messages:
alex: kicked off the 10k canary for quant-7b-v2 on runtime-v1.2. saw parse success drop when batch_size > 1. numbers: batch=1: 99.92% parse ok, batch=4: 96.14% parse ok. smoke logs below.

jin: can you paste a failing example?

alex: ```
{ "id": 12345, "action": "charge", "amount": 49.99 \u000E
# runtime returned ESC control and then stopped, missing closing brace
```

maria: hmm that looks like a control-char leak. is tokenizer on runtime same version as python tokeniser used in eval harness?

alex: runtime tokenizer = rust-tokenizer v0.9.1, harness tokenizer = python-tokenize v0.9.0. but weirdly only reproduces in int4 quant path + batching.

jin: try disabling continuous batching.

alex: turned continuous_batching=false for canary: batch=4 parse ok -> 99.9%. so batching interaction appears causal.

maria: hypothesis: batching reorder + kvcache map means some sequences get an extra sentinel byte from decoder path in int4 kernel. quant decode path uses raw byte slices and might not sanitize control bytes.

sam: options: 1) postprocess sanitizer that strips C0 control chars before parser 2) enforce anchor tokens around json (e.g. <JSON_START> ... <JSON_END>) 3) logit-bias enforce `}` token at end.

jin: postprocess sanitizer is cheap and safe. anchor tokens change prompts and may affect generation distribution. logit-bias is brittle across tokenizers.

alex: i'll run 10k canary with sanitizer enabled (pre-parser step: .replace(/\x00-\x1F/,'') ). also dump decode bytes for failures.

ci-bot: created job: https://ci.redwood/infra/canaries/1799993333 (status: queued)

maria: i'll prototype a small kernel-side decode-sanitize for int4 path, PR targetting runtime-v1.2-rc.

sam: assign: alex (canary run + failure artifacts), maria (kernel PoC), jin (parser sanitizer + unit tests). goal: reduce batch4 failure <0.5% by EOD.

alex: noted. starting run now. will post summary.

jin: thanks team :thumbsup:
